questions.question: Why is hard-coding a privileged API secret directly in a React Native app's JS code dangerous?
options: It isn't dangerous, since mobile apps are compiled binaries
The JS bundle ships inside the installed app package and can be extracted and read as plain JavaScript by anyone
JS code automatically encrypts itself when bundled for mobile
Only Android apps have this issue, not iOS
questions.explanation: Unlike compiled native code, the JS bundle is just (minified) JavaScript, extractable from the app package — anything in it should be treated as fully public.

questions.question: Why should an auth token be stored with something like react-native-keychain instead of AsyncStorage?
options: AsyncStorage persists data as unencrypted plain text on the filesystem, while Keychain/Keystore provide hardware-backed encrypted storage designed for credentials
Keychain is faster for all types of data
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explanation: AsyncStorage prioritizes simplicity over security; sensitive values like tokens need the OS-level secure storage that Keychain (iOS) and Keystore (Android) provide.

questions.question: What specific attack does certificate pinning defend against that plain HTTPS alone does not?
options: A man-in-the-middle attacker presenting a certificate that is technically valid (e.g. from a compromised or coerced certificate authority) but isn't the server's real certificate
questions.explanation: HTTPS alone trusts any certificate signed by a trusted CA; pinning adds a check against the server's actual known fingerprint, catching a validly-signed-but-wrong certificate.

questions.question: What operational risk does certificate pinning introduce?
options: None — it's entirely risk-free once implemented
If the server's real certificate is rotated without first shipping an app update with the new pinned fingerprint, the app will start rejecting legitimate connections
It makes all network requests significantly slower
It prevents the app from using HTTPS at all
questions.explanation: Pinning ties the app to a specific certificate fingerprint, so certificate rotation must be coordinated with an app release, or existing installs will start failing to connect.
